newsitem.title: UK: FORECAST-Imperial set for steady maiden results.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST-Imperial set for steady maiden results.

text.p: Britain's Imperial Tobacco Group Plc, is expected to report pre-tax profits of about 145 million stg for the half year on Wednesday in its first set of results since it demerged from Hanson Plc last October.
Brokers pre-tax profit forecasts range from 136 to 150 million. A dividend payout of 7.0p per share is expected.
Analysts expect the group's performance to be held back by the strength of sterling and a cigarette price war in France.
"Otherwise it's steady as she goes in terms of underlying performance," said one analyst, who chose not to be named.

Attention will also focus on Imperial's proposed acquisition of Netherlands-based Rizla International BV for 168 million stg in January. A decision on whether to let the deal through on monopolies grounds was delayed by the election announcement.

The acquisition of Rizla, the world's biggest maker of hand-rolling tobacco papers, is aimed at enhancing the group's international expansion. Rizla has a large market share in seven or eight European countries.
Analysts are keen to see the group expand out of Britain where tobacco sales are under pressure from the powerful health lobby group and relatively high tax duties.

The new incoming Labour government has also pledged in its manifesto to ban tobacco advertising which is expected to hit sales of premium brand cigarettes, like Silk Cut and Benson & Hedges, in favour of cheaper brands.

Imperial, owners of the John Player Special and Embassy brands, has about 38 percent of the British market. Gallaher, owned by American Brands Inc, holds the lion's share with 40 percent of tobacco sales in Britain, or 32 billion cigarettes a year.
Imperial shares were unchanged at 407p on Friday, against a high of 440p for the year.
